title: Practice designs in order: link shortener, rate limiter, chat, feed, retrieval service, agent platform

claims.text: The estimation figures that make each of these arguable are order-of-magnitude: a main memory reference around 100 nanoseconds, a datacenter round trip around 500,000, a disk seek around 10,000,000, and 1 megabyte read sequentially from disk around 30,000,000.

source.title: Jeffrey Dean, Large-Scale Distributed Systems at Google: Current Systems and Future Directions, keynote at LADIS 2009, October 2009 — the slide deck carrying Numbers Everyone Should Know

claims.text: Fan-out inherits the worst case: a server whose 99th percentile is one second, queried across 2,000 servers at even a one in ten thousand chance of slowness, leaves 18% of requests exceeding one second — which is why a design that queries many things needs an answer for the tail rather than for the average.

source.title: Jeffrey Dean and Luiz Andre Barroso, The tail at scale, Communications of the ACM 56(2):74-80, February 2013, doi 10.1145/2408776.2408794

claims.text: Serving a large model at high throughput requires batching, and batch size is limited by per-request cache memory that is huge and grows and shrinks dynamically — so the final design in this sequence is constrained by memory rather than by arithmetic.

source.title: Woosuk Kwon et al., Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention, Proceedings of the 29th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, 2023 (arXiv:2309.06180)

beats.broke: the track has covered every component separately, and knowing them separately is not the same as being able to assemble one under questioning
beats.fix: work a fixed sequence of designs in increasing order of difficulty, each adding exactly one new constraint over the last, so that what is being practised is assembly rather than recall
beats.cost: practising a sequence produces fluency in that sequence, so the value comes from being interrupted and pushed off the path rather than from completing it
beats.interview: which constraint each design in the sequence introduces
